source_caption:
How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days is one of the most beloved romantic comedies of the 2000s, combining sharp humor, undeniable chemistry, and a clever twist on the classic love story formula. Starring Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey, the film follows two people who enter a relationship with completely opposite hidden agendas.

Andie Anderson, a magazine writer, is working on an article about how to drive a man away in ten days, while advertising executive Ben Barry is trying to prove he can make any woman fall in love with him. Neither realizes they’re being used for the other’s challenge, setting the stage for a series of hilarious misunderstandings and increasingly ridiculous situations.

What makes the film endure is the chemistry between Hudson and McConaughey. Their playful banter and natural charisma elevate the story beyond a simple romantic comedy, making even the most absurd moments feel fun and charming.

Beneath the laughs, How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days is about authenticity. As the games and manipulation begin to fall apart, both characters are forced to confront who they really are and whether a relationship can survive once the masks come off. Funny, energetic, and endlessly rewatchable, it’s the kind of romantic comedy that continues to win over audiences years after its release.

source_details.synopsis: How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days is a 2003 romantic comedy film directed by Donald Petrie, from a script by Kristen Buckley, Brian Regan, and Burr Steers, and starring Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey. Loosely based on the picture book of the same name by Michele Alexander and Jeannie Long, the plot concerns a women's magazine writer and an advertising executive who both begin a relationship with ulterior motives. While the story and characters in the film are original, the dating "don'ts" of the picture book are included in the film.
